title: Gender and Agri-Energy in Uganda: Evidence, Gaps and Programming Recommendations
summary: Brief examining gender dimensions of agri-energy access, use, and enterprise in Uganda, with recommendations for gender-responsive programming.
description: Women in Uganda are central to agricultural production, food processing, and household energy management, yet they are frequently marginalised in agri-energy programming and rarely prioritised as technology users or enterprise owners. This brief reviews available evidence on gender and agri-energy in Uganda, documenting differences in access, use, benefit, and decision-making between women and men. It identifies specific high-impact entry points for gender-responsive programming — including women in solar milling enterprises, women's cold room cooperatives, gender-targeted biogas adoption support, and women-led clean cooking enterprises. The brief concludes with practical programming recommendations for donors, implementing partners, and government agencies.
